where: Section 3, sentence after the gain formulas
problem: It says the factor (πD/λ)² is 'roughly the number of square wavelengths filling the dish mouth'. That is wrong by a factor of 4π ≈ 12.6. The physical mouth area is πD²/4, so the number of square wavelengths it holds is (πD²/4)/λ² = 0.785 (D/λ)², while (πD/λ)² = 9.87 (D/λ)². For the 3 m dish at 4 GHz the mouth holds about 1257 square wavelengths but (πD/λ)² = 15,791. A student who trusts this sentence will mis-size the aperture.
fix: The factor (πD/λ)² equals 4π times the mouth area measured in square wavelengths: (πD/λ)² = 4π × (πD²/4)/λ². Equivalently, gain = η × 4π × (physical aperture area in square wavelengths).

problem: 'not at the centre of the dish surface' is confusing: the centre of the dish surface is the vertex, which is where the focus is measured from. As written it contradicts the first half of the sentence.
fix: The feed goes at the focus, a distance f in front of the vertex, not on the dish surface itself (not on the metal at the vertex). Sketches with the feed on the metal lose marks.
